result.environment: Windows Rust/C++ and real Steam client; Go 1.26.6 Windows/Linux; isolated PostgreSQL14 schemas47→48 and nonpersistent Redis. Each retained execution states its actual environment; no complete strict gameplay run.
result.command_or_harness: See owner report tests and the referenced exact command/output logs.
result.exit_code_note: Multiple evidence commands; individual exit codes are preserved in owner report tests. This is not one executed test command.
observed_result: Runtime serializes login/logout/redeem/session acquisition, revalidates the exact session epoch/token/SteamID before committing identity, and clears runtime identity even when remote logout fails. Account changes zeroize the old Steam ticket and AuthIdentity zeroizes it on drop. Account transition first drains player-owned launch/room/native work while its required credentials are still valid; cleanup failure retains that current session and returns AUTH_CLEANUP_PENDING before revocation. The frontend may restore only a freshly queried authenticated session for that explicit failure, never its old account snapshot after revocation. This complements CredentialsStore CAS and the executed concurrent HTTP tests; cross-machine native account-switch gameplay remains unrun. Public authenticated player requests retain the account-transition guard for the full operation. The independent match/status/room worker gates drain their in-flight network requests and compensation before account revocation. CommunityNode heartbeat retains separate ownership; its player-owned catalog sync uses a nonblocking transition guard and verifies the session epoch, while local stop needs no player token.

Online runtime token acquisition requires auth::ensure_authenticated and session_epoch/profile verification; offline PvE remains separate. Account switch, invitation redemption, and logout serialize through an auth transition gate: owned launch/match cleanup runs while the old credential is valid, including before redeem begin_session; cleanup failure preserves the old identity/resources and returns AUTH_CLEANUP_PENDING, and only successful cleanup reaches session replacement/revocation. A real auth failure reopens the temporary operation block while shutdown remains closed. Public player requests hold the transition gate for their full call and verify epoch; status/room/match supervisors are drained independently. CommunityNode heartbeat remains independent during player transitions, while its owned-account sync runs outside the tick lock only under a non-blocking auth-transition gate with before/after blocked, shutdown, and epoch checks. CommunityNode stop_local is token-free. Long-lived supervisors are retained for relogin and final shutdown joins them. Deterministic Rust tests and the final lib run pass, but real expired/revoked service responses were not run without a live service.

observed_result: LaunchOperation carries online role/Lobby/Attempt/session epoch, operation/run IDs, monotonic sequence and process-monotonic observation time. Cancellation targets the owned record even after the current lobby snapshot is gone, reaches the existing worker, is idempotent and does not fake a cleanup completion. An actual runtime regression verifies this ordering. Frontend account/operation/exit ordering tests are recorded by the Toolbox report. Complete per-phase native cancellation, cleanup and successive-attempt E2E remain unrun. Cleanup leases keep new starts blocked until owned game/transport/native cleanup finishes; retries perform the complete cleanup and failures remain scoped. Old IO cannot clear a newer receipt. A real duplicated Windows child handle supplies exited-process evidence for dead P2P authorities; a live or unverifiable process still requires an actual native pipe ACK. Pre-spawn controller/launcher failures retain exact Attempt scope and sealed not-started evidence. Every post-spawn failure retains a typed cleanup context; unavailable process proof remains quarantined rather than fabricating a not-started/exit receipt. The host_ready uncertainty retry first uses the exact world and permits empty-world owned-exit only after the specific backend MATCH_WORLD_INSTANCE_REQUIRED response. Final runtime shutdown retains the process-status scanner through KillTracked/resource reclamation, then sends its explicit Shutdown command and joins both that worker and its in-flight version probe. Account transitions do not stop the long-lived scanner. This lifecycle has a real-thread regression with a held synthetic version probe; native application-close acceptance remains separate.

PVE and MatchLobby online launches now use the same LaunchOperation store and get/cancel API. Match operations are bound to the current lobby, Attempt, and authorized host/member role; host, member, and route refresh share a cancellation token. Online process tracking records real PIDs, cancellation performs native/backend compensation and local safe cleanup before terminal status, and LaunchComplete/Succeeded is emitted only after strict Payload telemetry reaches the local player's Playable state. Public player operations hold the auth transition gate through controller I/O and epoch validation; live native/service cancellation and retry injection was not run in this agent task.

observed_result: LaunchOperation carries online role/Lobby/Attempt/session epoch, operation/run IDs, monotonic sequence and process-monotonic observation time. Cancellation targets the owned record even after the current lobby snapshot is gone, reaches the existing worker, is idempotent and does not fake a cleanup completion. An actual runtime regression verifies this ordering. Frontend account/operation/exit ordering tests are recorded by the Toolbox report. Complete per-phase native cancellation, cleanup and successive-attempt E2E remain unrun. Cleanup leases keep new starts blocked until owned game/transport/native cleanup finishes; retries perform the complete cleanup and failures remain scoped. Old IO cannot clear a newer receipt. A real duplicated Windows child handle supplies exited-process evidence for dead P2P authorities; a live or unverifiable process still requires an actual native pipe ACK. Pre-spawn controller/launcher failures retain exact Attempt scope and sealed not-started evidence. Every post-spawn failure retains a typed cleanup context; unavailable process proof remains quarantined rather than fabricating a not-started/exit receipt. The host_ready uncertainty retry first uses the exact world and permits empty-world owned-exit only after the specific backend MATCH_WORLD_INSTANCE_REQUIRED response. Final runtime shutdown retains the process-status scanner through KillTracked/resource reclamation, then sends its explicit Shutdown command and joins both that worker and its in-flight version probe. Account transitions do not stop the long-lived scanner. This lifecycle has a real-thread regression with a held synthetic version probe; native application-close acceptance remains separate.

Online complete_launch is staged without a success event while processes are merely tracked. The operation remains Running through authority/member reporting and Payload Playable telemetry; only then is the single terminal Succeeded emitted. Failures first enter cleanup_pending and the worker completes native/backend/local cleanup before Failed or Cancelled is recorded. Match action and status/room supervisors now expose drain gates to account cleanup. Runtime behavior tests pass; real process/network failure injection was not run in this agent task.

result.exit_code_note: Multiple evidence commands; individual exit codes are preserved in owner report tests. This is not one executed test command.
observed_result: LaunchOperation carries online role/Lobby/Attempt/session epoch, operation/run IDs, monotonic sequence and process-monotonic observation time. Cancellation targets the owned record even after the current lobby snapshot is gone, reaches the existing worker, is idempotent and does not fake a cleanup completion. An actual runtime regression verifies this ordering. Frontend account/operation/exit ordering tests are recorded by the Toolbox report. Complete per-phase native cancellation, cleanup and successive-attempt E2E remain unrun. Cleanup leases keep new starts blocked until owned game/transport/native cleanup finishes; retries perform the complete cleanup and failures remain scoped. Old IO cannot clear a newer receipt. A real duplicated Windows child handle supplies exited-process evidence for dead P2P authorities; a live or unverifiable process still requires an actual native pipe ACK. Pre-spawn controller/launcher failures retain exact Attempt scope and sealed not-started evidence. Every post-spawn failure retains a typed cleanup context; unavailable process proof remains quarantined rather than fabricating a not-started/exit receipt. The host_ready uncertainty retry first uses the exact world and permits empty-world owned-exit only after the specific backend MATCH_WORLD_INSTANCE_REQUIRED response. Final runtime shutdown retains the process-status scanner through KillTracked/resource reclamation, then sends its explicit Shutdown command and joins both that worker and its in-flight version probe. Account transitions do not stop the long-lived scanner. This lifecycle has a real-thread regression with a held synthetic version probe; native application-close acceptance remains separate.

Revalidated after the owned-process and preflight cleanup follow-ups: Backend accepts only exact attempt/session/world/roster/route scope; Dedicated and P2P HOST cleanup require exact evidence shapes. P2P owned_process_exited requires non-zero process_id plus win-filetime start fingerprint; native_process_not_started is only for a P2P HOST before Payload/world publication and requires empty process fields. Real isolated PostgreSQL runs rejected member/non-HOST, malformed evidence, old-world, stale-route, and installed-Payload preflight callbacks, then accepted the exact scoped receipts. Successful transitions persist non-secret scope/evidence metadata in the existing security-audit JSON stream without storing the bearer session. Actual OS child-handle/pre-spawn proof remains the Toolbox supervisor responsibility.

Clear/release validates exact allocation and native ownership. Old live disconnect cleans only its own scope and cannot clear a newer pending admission. Real one-client disconnect/release is observed; full delayed-stale-clear/reuse matrix remains unrun.

Connection events, cleanup ACKs, backend callbacks, cursor advancement, and cleanup scope require exact attempt/session/world/roster/route context; pending clear is retried. Pre-spawn provisioning failures seal NativeProcessNotStarted with the exact Attempt/session/roster/route scope and no process/pipe/PID evidence. Post-spawn authority failures retain the typed owned process/quarantine evidence and never fall back to PID zero or a fake not-started marker. No multi-attempt live callback injection was run.
